title: Constitutional Semantic Hashing: Governed Commitment Schemes for Semantic Provenance, Admissibility, and Constitutional Continuity
description_html:
Constitutional Semantic Hashing (CSH) is a governed commitment framework for governance-aware semantic systems. Rather than introducing a new cryptographic primitive, CSH composes existing audited cryptographic tools — including BLAKE3, SHA-256, Ed25519, deterministic canonicalization schemes, and lineage-aware receipt chains — with explicitly declared interpretation regimes, admissibility laws, authority contexts, and lineage continuity constraints.

The framework addresses a growing systems problem: byte-level identity is insufficient for systems requiring governance-relative continuity, provenance-aware identity, deterministic divergence detection, and admissibility-aware semantic evolution. Under CSH, hashes become commitments over declared equivalence classes under specified governance regimes rather than merely checksums of structural representation.

CSH introduces:

  • interpretation regimes as first-class governance objects,
  • admissibility-aware continuity semantics,
  • lineage-bound commitment relations,
  • deterministic divergence detection relative to declared regimes,
  • and governance-aware semantic identity.

The paper formalizes:

  • artifacts,
  • semantic lenses,
  • interpretation regimes,
  • admissibility laws,
  • authority,
  • and lineage continuity

within a governed commitment framework deployable as a thin governance layer over existing cryptographic stacks.

CSH is designed to compose naturally with:

  • semantic hashing systems,
  • provenance-aware infrastructure,
  • constitutional memory architectures,
  • MCIR,
  • CONDEX,
  • DKN,
  • and governance-bound AI systems.

The work is positioned as a systems-and-governance contribution rather than a novel cryptographic primitive, emphasizing mechanically verifiable regime-relative continuity and governance-aware semantic commitments.
